opened.title: Stop helping the compiler, plus another 1.9% of the game
opened.author: Veradictus
opened.untrustedBody:
## The part everyone will read

Turns out a few of our build steps were doing GCC 2.95's homework for it. Apparently a 25-year-old compiler is supposed to suffer alone, so now it does.

What's gone:
- `fix_tail_calls.py`, `fix_trunc_slot.py` and `fix_core_spills.py`, which touched up the compiler's output after the fact.
- Per-function flags. GCC 2.95 only takes flags per file, so now we do too (`config/file_cflags.txt`). Four level functions moved into files of their own to keep theirs. Level files are our own grouping anyway; retail never saw them.

We measured the damage before deleting anything. 12 functions depended on all of it: 2,404 bytes, 0.06% of the code. Seven still match with a whole-file flag. Five (620 bytes) are assembly again, including `_exit`, all 8 bytes of it, so `core/crt0` is no longer a complete unit. Our condolences to crt0.

The `ps2eeas` emulation stays, and now it comes with receipts. We never used SN's real assembler because it died with a stack o

merged.title: decomp: thirty shared native C families across the overlays
merged.author: llesieur99
merged.untrustedBody:
Integrate thirty shared native C families across the boot-adjacent overlays.

Each family enters the tree only when a single authored body reproduces the
exact reference bytes at every measured placement: 2,717 native placements are
compared complete and unmasked against the pinned images, plus every prior
control in the same 28 units.

Measured techniques this lot adds to the method notes:

* inside a straight-line body of constant stores, the first scheduler hoists the
  last statement, the store of a multi-instruction 64-bit constant and the last
  store of each floating constant group, then keeps source order — writing the
  source in the retail order with those statements moved to the end reproduces
  the retail schedule;
* a numeric address and an external symbol generate different code (the
  assembler folds a literal into the destination register), and which one
  matches is a measured property of each body.

Refusals stay on record with their measured census: small-data `$gp`

merged.author: llesieur99
merged.untrustedBody:
## What

Fifteen shared native families whose retail bodies address a global through
`$gp` are now carried by the **default unit** of every level program that places
them. Nothing about the existing unit changes: no new section, no new profile,
no new format, and not one patched byte.

Two reviewed inputs change instead:

* the level catalogue states the overlay's **measured gp base** (`0x001AEFF0`).
  The integration already accepted a native unit with a non-zero gp, so the
  mechanism was in the tree; what was missing was a reviewed body able to use it.
* the source declares each touched global with the attribute its **retail sites**
  require, measured per symbol from the reference disassembly:

| retail behaviour at that address | declaration |
| --- | --- |
| every access resolves through `$gp` | `__attribute__((sda))` |
| every access is absolute | `__attribute__((nosda))` |
| both forms occur at the same address | no attribute (the assembler decides per site) |

## Why it works

merged.author: llesieur99
merged.untrustedBody:
## What this lot binds

One authored C body per shared native family, with **every measured placement bound and verified
byte for byte** before anything is written into the tree. Fifty-two new families.

* Physical integrated C coverage: **498 200 → 525 580 bytes** (1.0211 % → 1.0773 %)
* Conservative unique matched C: **102 540 → 113 816 bytes** of 44 451 612 (0.2307 % → 0.2560 %)
* Overlay placements 7 143 → 7 335; native bodies 2 747 → 2 939; boot unit unchanged

## The lever that made these families reachable

The retail build compiled with cc1 modelling a small global access as **one** macro instruction
that gas expands per site. The pinned default profile materialises an explicit `lui`+`lw`
instead, which shifts register allocation and scheduling away from the retail bytes and makes
the promoted body a different size. Declaring the touched symbol `sda` restores the
one-instruction model; gas then chooses the encoding exactly as the retail build did — absolute
outside a `.set noma

merged.author: llesieur99
merged.untrustedBody:
## Why

An independent reproducibility study rebuilt the documented toolchain from the public recipe and got
a different compiler identity from the one `docs/COMPILER-NOTES.md` records:

| Identity | Documented | Their rebuild |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gcc/config/mips/mips.c` | `c76c0bec…` (282 066 B) | `a2c787dd…` (281 557 B) |
| `gcc/cc1` | `8bed6eae…` | `c84ca6f8…` |

Their compiler still reproduces the qualified boot object byte for byte (178/178 functions), so the
gap is not in the code — it is in the recipe.

**Cause.** The recipe described the five source adjustments in prose. Two of them are
text-carrying replacements whose annotation is part of the hashed identity, and the recipe never
gave their literal text:

* the TImode anchor becomes `  if (0 && TARGET_MIPS5900) /* RAC2 : ancre TImode neutralisee */`
* the ascending GPR save loop is a literal block whose comment begins `/* RAC2 : emission en ordre CROISSANT … */`

The annotations alone are 183 bytes; with the exact code sh

Their compiler still reproduces the qualified boot object byte for byte (178/178 functions), so the

Recorded trials require manual instruction comparison, and finishing a validated batch requires coordinating proof, catalogue, report, view and display commands. Add official `campaign.py diff` and `campaign.py finalize` commands backed by the campaign register and maintained exact validators.

The private interactive review shows complete-symbol R5900 instructions and every byte at exact addresses, with target/function selection and difference navigation. It verifies immutable artifacts, distinguishes historical and relocatable diagnostics, optionally serves one read-only loopback capability URL, and adds no acceptance or credit.

The finalizer validates a fresh passed boot/27-overlay action, compiler/SDK identities and pinned inputs, then regenerates boundaries, pointer and boot evidence, unique/physical/reuse reports, source inventory and campaign views in a private snapshot.
